title: Omni Documents are the Artifact's deliberate residual category for anything that does not map to a single Primitive
content:
A.6.1.1.8.3 defines Omni Documents as covering "Launch Agent 7's strategic intent and operational processes relating to infrastructure inherited from Sky Core, activities unrelated to Sky Primitives, or activities spanning multiple Sky Primitives."

Almost the entire Artifact is indexed by Primitive: each capability is a primitive, each use of it an Instance. That taxonomy is what makes the document machine-navigable, but it only works if every fact has a home. Three kinds of fact do not — inherited infrastructure that predates the Agent's own primitives, activity outside the primitive system altogether, and activity that cuts across several primitives at once.

Omni Documents are the named remainder bin for exactly those three. Naming the residual explicitly is the design choice worth extracting: an unnamed remainder would either force material to be filed under a primitive it does not belong to — corrupting the index — or push it out of the Artifact entirely, beyond the reach of Root Edit review.

The risk it carries is the usual one for catch-all categories: the third clause ("spanning multiple Sky Primitives") is broad enough to absorb a great deal, and material placed there is not organized by any further scheme. The Artifact's legibility depends on Omni staying small relative to the primitive tree.
description: They cover infrastructure inherited from Sky Core, activity unrelated to any Primitive, and activity spanning several — the escape hatch that keeps a Primitive-indexed document complete.
